payload.unsafe_pattern: recursive chmod (execa 'chmod -R a+rX' or equivalent) applied to a directory tree that also holds files intentionally created at 0o600 for sensitive audit/token content
payload.consequence: sensitive audit/token log files become world-readable, an information-disclosure defect
payload.mechanical_correction: scope chmod to the top-level directory and its direct files only, or create sensitive files with restrictive mode via fs.openSync+fchmodSync rather than relying on a later broad chmod pass

evidence.detail: token-persistence.js audit log moved from 0o644 to 0o600 with explicit openSync+fchmodSync; artifact-preservation.ts gained chmodRuntimeDir opt-out
removed recursive chmodRuntimeDir widening for API-proxy logs dir and removed proxyLogsDir from recursive fixArtifactPermissionsForRootless list
unresolved comment: container-stop.ts fixSquidLogPermissions still runs chmod -R a+rX on the shared /var/log/squid dir, re-exposing the 0600 audit file

payload.unsafe_pattern: recursive chmod/chown (or a broad-scope repair loop) applied to a directory tree that also holds files intentionally created at a restrictive mode for sensitive audit/token content
payload.consequence: a fourth confirmed occurrence reinforcing the existing rule: a squid-service startup preflight repair had to be kept scoped to an explicit top-level log-file list instead of a recursive chown/chmod pass, because /var/log/squid can share the host directory tree with restricted-mode API-proxy audit files

evidence.detail: Fix Squid log permission repair across topology restarts: PR body explicitly states the fix 'Keeps repair scoped to explicit top-level log files instead of recursive ownership changes' and 'Preserves the existing non-recursive preflight invariant' as regression coverage; src/services/squid-service.ts SQUID_LOG_FILES comment: 'Keep this explicit instead of globbing or recursive chowning so startup does not traverse user-provided proxy log directories.'

fixSquidLogPermissions() docstring explicitly documents the same rule: 'The repair is intentionally NOT recursive ... A recursive chmod would widen permissions on payload-bearing API-proxy diagnostics (e.g. token-tracker-audit.jsonl, created at mode 0600) before preserveCleanupArtifacts() gets a chance to apply its own directory-scoped repair.'

payload.note: no new merged defect in this 14-day window scoped to gh-aw-firewall introduces a *new* recursive-chmod regression; this transaction adds corroborating evidence (an explicit non-recursive-by-design fix plus a second in-repo code comment restating the invariant) to the rule already on file rather than creating a duplicate. src/artifact-permissions.ts:158 still contains an unresolved recursive 'chmod -R a+rwX /fix' inside a docker-exec shell string touching the same auditDir tree (the false negative noted by the prior refiner evaluation); left unresolved in this window.
